high.title: TDF Yield Goes Up on Rate Hike Bets as Inflation Stays Elevated
high.summary: The BSP's term deposit facility (TDF) auction saw notably weak demand, with bids totaling only P129.622 billion against P150 billion in seven-day papers offered — producing a bid-to-cover ratio of just 0.8, well below the previous week's P137.524 billion in tenders. The undersubscription signals that market participants are repricing BSP liquidity instruments higher in anticipation of further monetary policy tightening, driven by persistently elevated July inflation. For bond investors, this is a critical signal: rising TDF yields typically feed through to the broader government securities curve, pressuring sovereign bond prices lower. PHP traders should note that sustained rate hike expectations can provide near-term support for the peso by attracting carry interest, but also raise concerns about slowing economic growth. The BSP's next policy meeting will be closely watched for guidance on the tightening trajectory. Watch for: July CPI print confirmation, BSP Monetary Board forward guidance, and secondary market GS yield movements in the coming sessions.

high.title: Peso Surges as Iran Deal Hopes Hit Dollar
high.summary: The Philippine peso staged a sharp recovery on Wednesday, appreciating 41.4 centavos to close at P60.751 per USD — its strongest finish in nearly seven weeks, last seen at P60.567 on June 18. The move was driven primarily by broad-based USD weakness following reports of progress in US-Iran peace negotiations, which reduced geopolitical risk premiums and weighed on the dollar globally. The session opened stronger at P60.9, confirming directional momentum from the outset. For FX traders, this move is largely externally driven rather than a reflection of improving Philippine domestic fundamentals, which means sustainability depends heavily on geopolitical news flow. Key risks to the rally include a reversal in Iran deal sentiment, a hawkish Fed repricing, or renewed dollar demand from local importers. Watch for: USD/PHP resistance at P60.50–60.57 (June 18 level), any BSP intervention signaling, and whether the move attracts follow-through momentum from offshore positioning.

high.title: Bessent's Call to Upsize US Federal Reserve's Foreign Lending Facility May Not Be Risk-Free
high.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is pushing for an expansion of the Fed's Foreign and International Monetary Authorities (FIMA) repo facility, which allows official foreign accounts to borrow USD liquidity against US Treasury collateral. While the stated aim appears to support currency defense operations — notably for Japan — analysts warn the move carries significant risks, including incentivizing currency markets to test the resolve of Washington and Tokyo. For Philippine markets, an expanded FIMA facility has indirect but meaningful implications: it could strengthen the toolkit available to EM central banks, including the BSP, for managing FX volatility. However, it could also amplify USD liquidity dynamics globally, affecting emerging market capital flows. Any expansion would require Fed agreement, which remains uncertain. Watch for: Fed commentary on FIMA capacity, USD liquidity conditions, and spillover effects on PHP and BSP reserve management strategy.

high.title: July Inflation Cools to 4-Month Low
high.summary:
Philippine headline inflation decelerated to 6.2% in July from 6.4% in June, marking the slowest pace in four months (last seen at 4.1% in March). The moderation was driven by easing transport costs and stabilizing food inflation. While the trend is directionally encouraging, inflation at 6.2% remains substantially elevated relative to the BSP's target band (typically 2–4%), keeping the central bank in a challenging policy position. For PHP traders, cooling inflation could reduce pressure on the BSP to maintain an aggressive tightening stance, potentially signaling a pause or eventual pivot — a dynamic that may temper PHP support from the interest rate differential channel. For bond investors, softer CPI prints generally support lower yield expectations at the short end of the curve, potentially offering a rally opportunity in shorter-dated GS. The sharp year-on-year comparison (6.2% vs. 0.9% a year ago) underscores the base effect distortions at play. Watch for the BSP's August policy meeting and any guidance revisions in light of this data, as well as the forthcoming Q2 GDP release which could reinforce or complicate the easing narrative.

---

high.title: Peso Weakens Before Q2 GDP Data
high.summary: The Philippine Peso depreciated by 6.4 centavos on Thursday, closing at P60.815 per USD from the prior session's close of P60.751, as cautious market sentiment prevailed ahead of two key risk events: the release of Q2 Philippine GDP data and US labor market figures. Despite opening stronger at P60.68 and touching an intraday high of P60.58, the Peso reversed course and hit a low of P60.835 before settling near that level — suggesting selling pressure intensified through the session.

high.title: US Dollar to Retain Strength; Yen Intervention No Game Changer
high.summary:
Reuters-surveyed FX strategists expect the US dollar to maintain its strength over the coming months before a potential softening later in 2026. The yen briefly rallied approximately 4% against the dollar following coordinated intervention by Tokyo and Washington, but failed to reclaim prior intervention peaks — a signal that the structural USD bid remains intact. For PHP/USD traders, a persistently strong dollar environment is a direct headwind for the peso, likely keeping USD/PHP elevated in the near term. The BSP may face renewed pressure to defend the peso through FX intervention or verbal guidance should dollar strength persist. Bond investors should watch for pass-through inflation risks if PHP weakens further, which could complicate BSP's rate-cutting cycle. The key watchpoint is whether the Fed's policy trajectory shifts later in the year, which strategists appear to be pricing as the primary catalyst for eventual dollar softening. International fund managers should remain cautious on PHP longs and monitor USD momentum closely.

---

high.title: More BSP Rate Hikes Likely on Sticky Core Inflation
high.summary: Analysts, including Nomura Global Markets Research Chief ASEAN Economist Euben Paracuelles and Economist Nabila Amani, warn that the BSP's monetary tightening cycle is far from over despite headline inflation appearing to have peaked. The key concern is that core inflation — which strips out volatile food and energy prices — remains sticky and has not shown a broad-based decline. The softer July core print is assessed as likely temporary, as energy-sensitive commodities continue to exert upward pressure on underlying prices.

medium.title: PDIC Pushes Legislative Agenda to Boost Protection, Financial Stability
medium.summary:
The Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp. (PDIC) is seeking legislative amendments to expand deposit insurance coverage to nonbank financial institutions (NBFIs) and cooperatives, while also advocating for higher coverage limits for vulnerable depositor segments. PDIC President Roberto B. Tan outlined these priorities at a recent briefing, framing them as measures to strengthen consumer protection and systemic financial stability. While this is a regulatory and legislative development rather than an immediate market-moving event, broader NBFI inclusion in deposit insurance frameworks can enhance confidence in the shadow banking sector and reduce systemic contagion risk — a positive long-term signal for Philippine banking sector credit quality. Fund managers with exposure to Philippine bank equities or financial sector bonds should monitor legislative progress on this agenda.

---

medium.title: Stocks Slip as Risk-Off Mood Persists Before GDP
medium.summary: The PSEi declined 0.16% (−10.33 points) to close at 6,286.31, with the broader All Shares index also slipping 0.07% to 3,412.82, reflecting cautious positioning ahead of the Q2 GDP data release. Notably, the softer-than-expected July CPI print failed to provide a sustained lift to equities, as risk-off sentiment dominated market psychology. Easing global oil prices were insufficient to offset the prevailing caution. For equity investors, the market's muted response to a positive inflation surprise suggests near-term direction will be heavily anchored to the GDP outcome — a strong print could revive risk appetite and support a PSEi recovery, while a disappointment may extend the downside. Watch the GDP release closely as the key near-term catalyst.

medium.title: S&P Says Preemptive Measures to Shield Philippines from 'Super El Niño'
medium.summary: S&P Global Ratings has assessed that the Philippine government's early preparedness frameworks for the anticipated "Super El Niño" could limit macroeconomic damage, keeping the broader impact manageable across Asia-Pacific. This is a relevant macro risk signal for PHP and bond investors, as a severe El Niño episode historically pressures food inflation (upside CPI risk), disrupts agricultural output, and can widen the current account deficit by curbing agricultural exports while elevating import demand. S&P's relatively constructive view suggests sovereign credit metrics are unlikely to deteriorate sharply in the near term, which is supportive for Philippine sovereign bond spreads. However, investors should monitor weather developments closely as an intensifying El Niño could reignite food price pressures and complicate the BSP's nascent easing path.

medium.title: PDIC Eyes Return of P107-B Remittance to Augment Its Deposit Insurance Fund
medium.summary:
The Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp. (PDIC) is actively working to recover P107.23 billion in funds it remitted to the national government in 2025 under a budget provision subsequently struck down by the Supreme Court, with the goal of rebuilding its deposit insurance fund. The PDIC President confirmed coordination is underway with relevant government agencies to facilitate the recovery. This is a meaningful banking sector development: the adequacy of the deposit insurance fund is a key pillar of financial system stability, and its depletion raises contingent fiscal risks. For bond investors, a larger and better-capitalized PDIC reduces systemic risk premiums in the Philippine banking sector, which is broadly supportive of credit spreads. The successful recovery of these funds would be a positive signal for banking sector confidence and regulatory credibility.

---

medium.title: Jobless Rate Hits 3-Month High in June as More Filipinos Join Workforce
medium.summary: The Philippine unemployment rate climbed to 4.9% in June — a three-month high — up sharply from 3.7% a year earlier, with 2.59 million Filipinos currently out of work, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority. The uptick from May's 4.8% reflects a larger labor force participation rather than pure job destruction, though weakening labor conditions could weigh on household consumption and dampen GDP momentum. For BSP watchers, softer domestic demand dynamics may reinforce the case for continued monetary easing, potentially supportive of Philippine government bonds. However, sustained peso weakness and any inflation rebound could limit the BSP's room to maneuver. PSEi investors should note potential drag on consumer-facing sectors if spending softens.

medium.title: Philippine Farm Output Growth Slows in Q2
medium.summary: Agricultural sector growth decelerated sharply to 2.9% year-on-year in Q2 2026, down from 6% in the same period last year, with the value of farm and fisheries output rising to P452.22 billion at constant 2018 prices. While all subsectors registered positive growth, the notable slowdown is a mild negative signal for overall GDP performance and could have downstream implications for food inflation — a key variable the BSP monitors closely in its inflation targeting framework. Any renewed food price pressures stemming from softer agricultural supply growth could constrain the BSP's easing bias and weigh on PHP sentiment if inflation expectations drift higher. This data point warrants monitoring alongside the upcoming CPI release.

medium.title: First-Quarter GDP Growth Unchanged at 2.8%
medium.summary: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) confirmed Q1 2026 GDP growth at 2.8%, with no revision from the initial estimate. However, Gross National Income growth was revised downward to 2.9% from 3.0%, driven by a reduction in net primary income from abroad — a figure that captures OFW remittance flows and investment income — which was cut to 3.5% from 4.5%. The softer GNI revision is mildly negative for PHP as it suggests slightly weaker external income inflows than previously estimated. While the GDP headline is neutral, the subdued growth environment — particularly alongside sticky inflation — complicates the BSP's policy calculus and may dampen foreign investor enthusiasm for Philippine risk assets in the near term.

medium.title: PSEi Slips Further Before Philippine GDP Data Release
medium.summary: The PSEi fell 0.13% or 8.36 points to close at 6,277.95, extending its recent decline as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of the GDP data release. The broader All Shares Index edged marginally higher by 0.02%. The market's risk-off posture reflects uncertainty around the growth outlook, which is relevant for fund managers assessing the interplay between weak equity momentum and the BSP's tightening bias. A sustained PSEi below the 6,300 level warrants monitoring for potential foreign equity outflows that could add mild depreciation pressure on the PHP.
